title: Sierra Payments — Infosec Q&A and Evidence Digest
content:
Executive summary:

This document bundles our written responses to Sierra Payments' security questionnaire, maps Redwood controls to the customer's requirements (PCI-DSS and common enterprise controls), and indexes the evidence artifacts we collected for the Dedicated POC (VPC+HSM). It was compiled after the 2026-02-10 technical workshop and the follow-up evidence collection run on 2026-02-15. Purpose is to provide a single digest for Sierra's infosec reviewers and for internal audit handoff.

Scope and assumptions:
- Product surface: Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) deployed into customer VPC using our Private control plane.
- In-scope data: cardholder data (PAN, truncated/hashed tokens) in transit and at-rest within the customer VPC. Redwood control plane metadata (non-sensitive) remains in Redwood-hosted control plane unless explicitly configured for private control plane.
- Endpoint variants documented: TLS-terminated API frontends (mutual TLS option), model serving hosts (GPU instances), KMS/HSM for key wrapping, observability agents (prometheus + vector) sending logs to customer log collector.

High-level answers to key Sierra questions (summary):
1) Is PAN ever persisted on Redwood-managed storage outside the customer's VPC?
  - No. For the Dedicated POC we configured all tokenization and persistent storage to be customer-managed within the VPC. Control reference: Evidence items 002, 005.
2) How are keys managed and where are they stored?
  - Customer KMS-backed keys (AWS KMS) were configured for at-rest encryption with envelope encryption. For the POC we demonstrated PKCS#11-backed HSM integration for signing and key wrapping; HSM logs captured in evidence item 008.
3) What are the network boundaries and flow controls?
  - All model-serving traffic for the POC stayed within the customer VPC. Control plane connectivity used a single egress NAT gateway under customer control. We provided VPC flow logs and network ACLs in Evidence 003 and 004.
4) Can Redwood support canary rollbacks and fail-open policies without exposing secrets?
  - Yes. Rollouts are orchestrated by our private control-plane agent which supports signed artifacts and image verification. Rollback artifacts are stored in customer's S3 bucket when requested; verification proofs are included in Evidence 011.

Control mapping (concise):
- PCI-DSS (v4.0) mapping highlights:
  - Requirement 3.4 (PAN storage/encryption): Envelope encryption with customer KMS + HSM used for wrapping (evidence: 002, 008).
  - Requirement 7 (access control): Role-based access via IAM + OIDC; documented session recordings for admin ops in Evidence 006.
  - Requirement 10 (logging/monitoring): Centralized logs delivered to customer SIEM; sample log export + retention config in Evidence 004 and 009.
  - Requirement 11 (vulnerability scanning): Weekly container scans during POC; scan reports in Evidence 010.

Evidence index (artifacts and short descriptions):
- EVID-001: Sierra-POC-scope-and-config.yaml — POC configuration manifest (KMS ARNs redacted for public copy).
- EVID-002: disk-encryption-policy-and-kms-usage.pdf — screenshots and KMS policy demonstrating envelope encryption.
- EVID-003: vpc-flow-logs-sample-2026-02-14.txt — sanitized flow log slices showing internal-only traffic.
- EVID-004: log-delivery-config.json — vector/promtail config used to push logs to customer's ELK cluster.
- EVID-005: storage-permissions-audit.csv — S3 bucket ACLs and object ownership mapping for persistent model caches.
- EVID-006: admin-iam-roles-and-session-recording-links.txt — list of operator roles plus session trancripts (ops redacted links).
- EVID-007: mTLS-setup-guide-and-certs.pdf — steps we followed to enable mutual TLS for API ingress.
- EVID-008: hsm-integration-activity.log — PKCS#11 operations during the POC (wrapping operations timestamps).
- EVID-009: sample-alerts-and-retention-policy.md — alerting rules and retention settings configured for Sierra POC.
- EVID-010: container-scan-report-week-6.pdf — representative vulnerability scan showing no critical/high in runtime images.
- EVID-011: rollout-signature-proofs.tar.gz — signatures for artifacts and rollback proofs (manifest included).

Notes on sensitive evidence handling:
- The evidence bucket is encrypted with customer-managed CMKs; outbound sharing copies were redacted. Access is currently restricted to the RedTeam and Sierra's security contacts. We provided checksums and signing metadata (EVID-011) rather than raw secrets.

Open questions / action items raised in the workshop (owner and ETA):
- Q1: Sierra wants a short-lived ephemeral token flow for admin operations instead of long-lived IAM keys. Action: Draft ephemeral credential flow (Marcus) — ETA 2026-02-25.
- Q2: Confirmation requested on logs retention SLA (45 vs 90 days). Action: Ops to confirm retention pricing (Anya) — ETA 2026-02-20.
- Q3: Clarify whether tokenized PAN will be sent back in event responses. Action: Solutions engineering to provide sample response model (Lina) — ETA 2026-02-22.

Workshop notes (2026-02-10, technical deep dive):
- Attendees: Sierra security (J. Morales, K. Singh), Sierra infra (A. Brown), Redwood: Marcus Chen, Anya Patel, Lina Rodriguez, Ethan Williams.
- Key decisions: Use customer-managed KMS, HSM for wrapping; flows must avoid persistent PAN outside VPC; mutual TLS mandated for admin endpoints.
- Demonstrations performed: Live HSM wrap/unwrap, VPC-only model inference, log forwarding to customer ELK, container CVE scan.
- Follow-ups: Provide a hardened runbook for operational recovery and a signed artifact registry (covered in Evidence 011).

Internal audit notes (for Redwood SRE/security handoff):
- Attachments referenced in EVID-002, EVID-003, and EVID-008 should be pulled into the internal compliance folder under s3://redwood-evidence/sierra-payments/ with restricted ACLs.
- Recommend a short internal pre-audit checklist (will produce separate doc) covering: KMS key rotation proof, HSM tamper logs export, and retained session recordings for admin ops.

Appendix A — Redacted sample config snippets (excerpt):
- aws_kms_key_arn: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/EXAMPLE
- hsm_pkcs11_module: /usr/lib/softhsm/libsofthsm2.so
- vpc_subnet_ids: [subnet-0a1b2c3d, subnet-0d3c2b1a]  (redacted in public bundle)

- Current version (this digest) assembled 2026-02-18 and delivered to Sierra security channel.

If reviewers need direct unpacked artifacts for an onsite audit, contact security@redwood.ai to request short-term access tokens and a temporary read-only S3 pre-signed manifest.

End of digest.
